cards.name: Hairline Outline
cards.summary: One-click command button in the Outline Pen flyout that sets the outline of the selected objects to Hairline, CorelDRAW's thinnest preset outline width. It is a command, not a tool mode: it runs once and the active tool stays the same.
cards.how: Select one or more objects with the Pick tool, open the Outline Pen flyout in the toolbox and click Hairline Outline. Only the width changes; outline colour and style stay as they were. To set any other width, use Outline Pen (F12) or the outline width box on the property bar.
cards.script_api: Run the button with FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("1a7d5259-ae16-44e1-9a0c-13a7d4ef26a5") after selecting the shapes. Or set a width on the object model (Shape.Outline.Width, or Outline.SetProperties): that route needs no selection and opens no dialog, but the harvest gives no numeric Hairline width, so use the button when the exact Hairline preset is wanted.
use_for: cut lines for laser, vinyl or plotter cutting jobs that expect the thinnest outline
technical drawings and diagram linework at minimum weight
die-line and keyline layers in packaging files
showing guide or construction shapes thinly without hiding them
avoid: final print artwork where lines must reproduce: a hairline can come out faint or vanish on press, so use Outline Pen to set a real width
when the outline should get thicker as the object is scaled up: Hairline is a fixed preset width, so set a width in Outline Pen and turn on scaling with the object
running it with nothing selected: CorelDRAW then treats the change as a change to the document defaults and usually asks first in a dialog, which blocks an unattended script

review.changes: script_api: InvokeItem call written as FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem; noted that the object-model route has no harvested Hairline width value.

cards.name: No Outline
cards.summary: One-click command button in the Outline Pen flyout that removes the outline from the selected objects, so only their fill shows. It runs once and does not change the active tool.
cards.how: Select the objects with the Pick tool, open the Outline Pen flyout in the toolbox and click No Outline. The fill is untouched. Right-clicking the X (none) swatch on the colour palette does the same job. To get an outline back, set a width in Outline Pen or click Hairline Outline.
cards.script_api: Run the button with FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("aa134968-357f-4a06-b699-8b10e779a4f7") on the current selection. Or call Shape.Outline.SetNoOutline on each shape: no selection is needed and no dialog opens.
use_for: clean flat-colour shapes for icons, logos and illustrations
removing the default black outline from newly drawn rectangles, ellipses and other shapes
PowerClip frames holding photos that should show no border
text that was given an outline and needs it gone so small copy stays legible
avoid: shapes with no fill as well: they turn invisible and are easy to lose, so check fill first or use wireframe view to find them
when only a thinner line is wanted: use Hairline Outline or Outline Pen instead
running it with nothing selected: it then changes the document defaults (usually after a confirmation dialog) rather than any object

review.changes: use_for: dropped "traced objects" (PowerTRACE output already has no outline), reworded the bitmap item to PowerClip frames (placed bitmaps carry no outline) and the text item (text has no outline by default); script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem.

cards.name: Outline Color
cards.summary: Command button that opens CorelDRAW's Outline Color dialog to pick the outline colour of the selected objects from colour models, mixers or palettes. Width and line style stay unchanged.
cards.how: Select the objects, then click Outline Color in the Outline Pen flyout or press Shift+F12. Pick a colour model (CMYK, RGB, Lab ...), a palette swatch or a mixer value, type exact values if needed and click OK. For quick changes, right-click a colour-palette swatch instead. The full Outline Pen dialog (F12) holds colour together with width and style.
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("51c5cbff-f419-4a9d-90b0-c60d8445887b") only opens the modal dialog, which then needs a person. A script sets the colour directly instead: Shape.Outline.Color (a Color object, e.g. set with Color.CMYKAssign or Color.RGBAssign).
use_for: outline colours set to exact CMYK or spot values for print
matching outline colours to a brand palette
coloured keylines and borders on labels, badges and stickers
avoid: unattended scripts: the dialog is modal and blocks automation, so set Outline.Color through the object model instead
opening it with nothing selected: the colour then becomes a document default for new objects (usually after a confirmation dialog) and changes no existing object
changing width, dash style or arrowheads as well: Outline Color sets only the colour, so use Outline Pen (F12), which holds colour, width and style together

review.changes: equivalents: added AI Window/Color (Adobe Color Palette, sets stroke colour by colour model; it exists in the AI harvest, contrary to the writer note); avoid: replaced the unsupported claim that a colour alone may not make a line appear on a No Outline object; script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem.

cards.name: Outline Pen
cards.summary: Command button that opens the Outline Pen dialog, where every outline property of the selected objects is set in one place: colour, width, dash style, corners, line caps, position (outside, centred, inside), arrowheads, calligraphic nib shape, behind fill and scale with object.
cards.how: Select the objects and click Outline Pen in the toolbox flyout or press F12. Set width and units, colour, line style or a custom dash, corner and cap shape, and outline position. Add start and end arrowheads for open paths. Stretch and angle the nib for a calligraphic line. Tick Behind fill so a thick outline does not eat into text, and Scale with object so the width follows resizing. Click OK.
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("0203e4a7-f99a-4531-ae28-4160582d2f54") only opens the modal dialog. A script sets the same properties on the object model instead: Shape.Outline (Width, Color, Style, LineCaps, LineJoin, Justification for the inside/centre/outside position, StartArrow, EndArrow, BehindFill, ScaleWithShape), or Outline.SetProperties for several at once.
use_for: dashed cut or fold lines on packaging and die-lines
arrows and leader lines in diagrams, maps and instructions
thick outlined poster and sticker text with Behind fill on so the letterforms stay clean
calligraphic line art with a stretched, angled nib
logos whose outline must keep its proportion when scaled (Scale with object)
avoid: unattended scripts: the dialog is modal and blocks automation, so set Shape.Outline properties directly
one-off quick width or colour changes: the property bar outline width box or a right-click on a palette swatch is faster
relying on a heavy outline for a hard cut-out shape in output to other apps: convert the outline to an object first (Object > Convert Outline to Object) so it exports predictably

review.changes: script_api: added Outline.Justification (outline position, which the summary mentions); InvokeItem call written as FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem.

cards.name: Free Transform
cards.summary: Tool in the Pick tools flyout for rotating, mirroring, scaling and skewing selected objects by dragging around a pivot point you click, instead of using the fixed selection handles.
cards.how: Select objects, pick Free Transform from the Pick flyout and choose a mode on the property bar: Free rotation, Free angle reflection, Free scale or Free skew. Click where the pivot should be and drag. Rotation turns the objects round that point. Reflection mirrors them across the line you drag. Scale and skew stretch from that point. Turn on Apply to duplicate on the property bar to transform a copy and keep the original. The property bar also accepts exact angle, size and position values.
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("a7119a39-ad15-47d8-b06f-7f29617bfc0f") only switches to the tool; the harvest shows Application.ActiveTool reads -1 for it, so it has no ActiveTool value. The drag itself cannot be scripted. A script transforms the objects instead with Shape or ShapeRange methods: Rotate / RotateEx (rotate round a point), Skew / SkewEx, SetSize and Stretch, Flip for horizontal or vertical mirrors, AffineTransform for a mirror across an angled axis, plus Duplicate for the apply-to-duplicate case.
use_for: mirroring a shape across an angled axis for symmetric logos and ornaments
rotating elements around a chosen point, e.g. clock ticks, petals or radial patterns with Apply to duplicate
skewing text or panels for a quick isometric or italic slant
eyeballed scaling from a corner or a point outside the object
avoid: exact numeric transforms: use the property bar fields or the Transform docker instead of dragging
perspective or envelope distortion: Free Transform only does affine changes, so use the Perspective or Envelope effects
simple moves and handle scaling: the Pick tool is quicker

review.changes: script_api: Flip only mirrors horizontally or vertically, so added AffineTransform for the angled reflection the tool does; InvokeItem call written as FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem.

cards.name: Freehand Pick
cards.summary: Selection tool in the Pick flyout that selects objects by drawing a freeform, lasso-like marquee around them instead of a rectangle. Once objects are selected it moves and scales them like the Pick tool.
cards.how: Choose Freehand Pick from the Pick flyout and drag a freeform loop around the objects you want. Objects fully inside the loop are selected. Holding Alt while dragging is meant to also select objects the loop only touches (the Pick tool's touch-select modifier; not confirmed in the harvest for this tool). Hold Shift to add to or remove from the current selection. Then drag the selection or its handles as with Pick.
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("fb9a380a-4bbb-23bd-4e45-2eeed3e485b1") makes it the active tool. Application.ActiveTool = 1 (cdrToolPick) shares its state with Pick, and the toolbox then shows whichever Pick-flyout member was used last. A freeform drag cannot be scripted. A script selects by query instead (e.g. Shapes.FindShapes, then ShapeRange.CreateSelection).
use_for: picking scattered objects out of crowded illustrations or maps where a rectangle would catch neighbours
selecting irregular clusters of icons, shapes or text pieces in a dense layout
quick grab of objects along a diagonal or curved arrangement
avoid: selecting objects inside groups or behind others: use Pick with Ctrl-click or Alt-click, or the Objects docker
selecting nodes of a curve: use the Shape tool, which picks nodes, not whole objects
scripted selection: select by object properties in the object model, not with this tool

review.changes: script_api: InvokeItem call written as FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem; rest checked against the batch (shared state 5f85cce2, ActiveTool = 1) and left as is.

cards.name: Pick
cards.summary: CorelDRAW's main selection tool: click or drag a rectangular marquee to select objects, then move them, scale them with the handles, or click again to get rotate and skew handles.
cards.how: Click an object to select it. Shift-click adds or removes objects. Drag a marquee to select everything fully inside it, or hold Alt while dragging to also take objects the marquee touches. Ctrl-click selects an object inside a group, Alt-click selects the object behind. Drag to move, drag corner handles to scale proportionally and side handles to stretch. Click the selection a second time to switch to rotate and skew handles, and drag the centre marker to move the pivot. The property bar shows exact position, size, scale and angle.
cards.script_api: Application.ActiveTool = 1 (cdrToolPick) or FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("f1aee54d-c9aa-4e6f-9193-82f496b0b72b") makes it the active tool. Pick shares tool state 5f85cce2-041c-11d4-b32e-00a0c9e8a837 with Freehand Pick, so after ActiveTool = 1 the toolbox may show Freehand Pick. Clicks and drags cannot be scripted. A script does the same jobs on the object model: Shape.CreateSelection / AddToSelection, ActiveSelection, Shape.Move / SetPosition, SetSize, Rotate and Skew.
use_for: selecting, moving and resizing every kind of object in a layout: posters, flyers, business cards, packaging
precise placement through the property bar's position and size fields
rotating and skewing objects round their own centre or a dragged pivot
the default tool to return to between other tools
avoid: editing the shape of a curve or its nodes: use the Shape tool
irregular selections in crowded artwork: Freehand Pick or the Objects docker picks more precisely
transforms round an arbitrary point or along an angled mirror axis: Free Transform is easier

review.changes: script_api: InvokeItem call written as FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem; rest checked against the batch and left as is.
